title: The integral stratum bound
statement:
In the situation of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion],

$$
\Ext^q_{\mathcal O_E}(a_!L_0,b_!M_0)=0\quad(q>\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2),
$$

Ext taken in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Put Q=i_*u_!L₀, N=kb_*vb_!M₀ and K_n=Res_n(kb_*vb_!(M₀/π^(n+1))). Apply the supported lattice reduction-tower theorem. Its first Roos triangle gives N → P → P → N[1], where P is the product of the K_n and the middle map is 1 minus the quotient transition shift. Use only this triangle and the canonical levelRestrictionIso; the sections tower is not needed.

For each n and integer r, apply the finite-comparison theorem at exponent n+1 to the finite supported quotient. Compose its three natural abelian-group isomorphisms and use the scalar-restriction shift comparison and levelRestrictionIso. This identifies Hom(Q,K_n[r]) with H^r of the torsion stratum complex. Clause (2) of the torsion bound makes this group zero whenever cd_ℓ(j)+cd_ℓ(S)+1 < r.toNat.

Write d=cd_ℓ(j)+cd_ℓ(S). If d is infinite the given inequality is impossible. Otherwise regard d as a natural number; d+2<q.toNat implies d+1<(q-1).toNat and d+1<q.toNat. The preceding step kills Hom(Q,K_n[q-1]) and Hom(Q,K_n[q]) for every n. Shifts are equivalences and preserve products, so product extensionality kills Hom(Q,P[q-1]) and Hom(Q,P[q]). Shift the Roos triangle by q-1. Exactness of Hom(Q,-) says every map Q → N[q] annihilated in P[q] factors through P[q-1]. The latter Hom group is zero, so every map Q → N[q] is zero. This is the fiber-of-1-minus-shift argument for the one-degree derived-limit bound, without constructing the Milnor short exact sequence.

proof_origin.place: Lattices, Torsion targets and Integral targets. Apply Hom directly to the reduction Roos triangle already supplied by the supported-lattice tower lemma; the last paragraph of Integral targets identifies this fiber-of-1-minus-shift proof of the one-degree loss.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the situation of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion],

$$
\Ext^q_{\mathcal O_E}(a_!L_0,b_!M_0)=0\quad(q>\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2),
$$

Ext taken in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text:
*Completeness of the target.* By parts (3) and (4) of [sk-lem-integral-models], $b_!M_0$ lies in
$\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, so it is derived complete. Since $b_!$ is exact and $M_0$ is $\pi_E$-torsion
free, $b_!M_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n=b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)$; thus
$b_!M_0=R\varprojlim_nb_!(M_0/\pi_E^n)$.

*Completeness of $F$.* Put $F=L_0^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z\,b_!M_0$. By
[sk-lem-formal-closed-support-ii], each functor in this composite commutes with derived inverse limits
of sequences. Each also commutes with reduction modulo $\pi_E^n$, the cone of multiplication by
$\pi_E^n$, being exact and $\mathcal O_E$-linear. Hence

$$
F=R\varprojlim_nF_n,\qquad F_n=F\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n
=(L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n)\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z\,b_!(M_0/\pi_E^n).
$$

*Global sections.* $R\Gamma(S,-)$ is a right adjoint, so it preserves products, and it is exact, so it
preserves derived inverse limits of sequences. By part (2) of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support] (with
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$),

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L_0,b_!M_0)=R\Gamma(S,F)=R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(S,F_n).
$$

*The bound.* Put $c=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+1$. By
[det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion], $H^qR\Gamma(S,F_n)=0$ for $q>c$. The Milnor sequence

$$
0\to\varprojlim^1_nH^{q-1}R\Gamma(S,F_n)\to H^qR\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(S,F_n)\to\varprojlim_nH^qR\Gamma(S,F_n)\to0
$$

(the derived limit is the fiber of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on a product, and products of abelian groups are
exact; Stacks, Tag 08TB) shows that $H^q$ of the limit vanishes as soon as $q>c$ and $q-1>c$, i.e. for
$q>c+1$. This is the claim.
